subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up (PayWave)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up (PayWave)

Hi Catherine —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the sizing inputs we discussed. Please confirm or correct anything I’ve captured below so our infra team can produce a dedicated capacity recommendation.

What we heard from you:
- Primary use case: real-time PBV fraud scoring and transaction enrichment called synchronously from your API (99th percentile latency requirement ~200ms).
- Expected volume: ~1,200 TPS peak across North America (evening batch spikes), baseline ~400 TPS.
- Typical request profile: short prompts (system+user ~150 tokens), but occasional long-context flows (up to 2,000 tokens) for enriched customer history.
- Concurrency: roughly 400 concurrent requests at peak (most are small); bursts to 700+ for promo events.
- Data residency: must run in our VPC in us-east-1 (dedicated capacity preferred over hosted API for predictable SLAs).

Open clarifying items for sizing: 
1) Token mix: can you share approximate percent split between short requests (<200 tokens) vs long requests (>1k tokens)? You mentioned ~85% short, 15% long — can you confirm?
2) Latency SLO: 99th percentile 200ms — is that strict for long-context requests as well or only for short prompts?
3) Preferred GPU families: do you have an existing standard (A100 vs H100) or are you flexible to recommendations based on cost vs latency?

Next steps I propose:
- Rafael to share a preliminary capacity estimate for A100 vs H100 options (tokens/sec and concurrent models per GPU).
- We’ll send a short token-mix CSV and a sizing worksheet (attached) — if you can populate the token distribution and traffic schedule we’ll finalize numbers.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up with your DevOps next week to confirm network/inbound throughput limits.

Attachments: Dedicated_Capacity_Sizing_Sheet.xlsx (worksheet), paywave_token_mix.csv (blank template)

Thanks — appreciate the quick confirmation so we can move to a formal proposal.

Best,

Thanks Aditya — this looks right overall. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Token mix: confirmed 80-85% short (<200 tokens), 10-15% medium (200-1k), ~5% long (>1k). I attached a filled token-mix CSV.
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile 200ms applies to short and medium requests. For long requests we can accept up to 500ms p99 as they’re less latency-sensitive.
- GPU preference: we don’t have an internal standard. Cost is important, but if H100 materially reduces p99 latency for our medium workloads we’d consider it.

We’re happy to set a 30-min call with our DevOps on Monday 3/22 at 10am PT — looping them into this thread.

Catherine

Catherine.Li@paywave.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Catherine Li <catherine@paywave.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-19T13:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up (PayWave)

Hi Catherine — thanks for the token mix and the call slot. I did a quick back-of-envelope to illustrate how GPU choices and batching affect throughput and p99 for your profile. Below are conservative estimates for production-ready configs (we’ll refine after we get your filled worksheet and traffic schedule):

Assumptions:
- Model: open-llm/gpt-13b (production equivalent you mentioned)
- Avg short request: 150 tokens (prompt+response combined)
- Avg medium: 600 tokens
- Avg long: 1,800 tokens
- Batch policy: latency-sensitive requests will use small batch window (20-30ms) for p99 preservation; background long requests can be batched more aggressively.

Preliminary sizing (per-GPU):
- NVIDIA A100 80GB (fp16/quantized path): ~6,000 short-request TPS equivalent (small-batch optimized), p99 ~180-220ms for short requests at 250 concurrent small streams. For mixed load including medium/long, effective throughput drops (medium ~1,500 TPS equivalent, long ~450 TPS equivalent).
- NVIDIA H100 80GB: ~9,000 short-request TPS equivalent (better kernel perf), p99 ~120-160ms for short requests at 250 concurrent small streams; medium/long similarly higher capacity.

Capacity recommendation for PayWave (peak 1,200 TPS with 85/10/5 token split and bursts to 1,800 TPS):
- A100 option (cost-optimized): 4 x A100 80GB GPUs (allows headroom for bursts and autoscaling + redundancy). Expected to meet p99 200ms for short/medium with tuned batching and KV caching.
- H100 option (latency-optimized): 3 x H100 80GB GPUs (lower instance count, better p99 headroom). Recommended if you prioritize latency and want fewer machines to manage.

Concurrency & configuration notes:
- Concurrency target: configure request routing for ~400-500 concurrency per model instance cluster; Redwood runtime will shard and route to preserve p99.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for frequent short prompts (we typically see 25-40% token savings for repeated system prompts).
- Autoscaling: reserve 20-30% spare capacity to absorb promo spikes; we can configure warm standby nodes.

Next steps I’ll take:
- Produce a short comparativesheet (A100 vs H100 total cost estimate + expected p99 numbers) and attach to the drive link.
- After the Monday DevOps call, we’ll finalize the sizing worksheet and provide a recommended Dedicated Capacity SKU and bill of materials.

Attachments referenced: Dedicated_Capacity_Sizing_Sheet.xlsx (we’ll update with GPU rows), paywave_token_mix.csv (received)

Let me know if you want me to include an option with half the GPUs but more aggressive quantization (lower cost, slight risk to output-quality).

—Rafael
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com
